campaign.title: Small Hours
campaign.hook: Nothing much happens. A kettle breaks. Somebody has a birthday. It rains on the hull. Standalone moments aboard, for when you want something quiet, or between stories.

episodes.title: The kettle
text: The kettle breaks. It has been making the ship's tea for longer than anyone aboard has been alive, and this morning it simply stops.

Nobody says anything for a moment. Then {Crew} takes it apart on the galley table, with tiny screwdrivers and enormous patience, while everyone else makes tea in a saucepan, which is wrong in every possible way.
By evening, the kettle works again. It whistles a slightly different note now. Everyone agrees it suits it.

episodes.title: Rain on the hull
text: The ship parks in the clouds of a gas giant for the night, and it rains: real rain, made of something warm, drumming on the hull.
Everyone ends up in the galley with blankets, not talking much, listening to it. {Crew} falls asleep sitting up. Nobody wakes {crew.them}.

episodes.title: A birthday
text: It is {Crew}'s birthday, and {crew.they} {crew:hasn't|haven't} told anyone, and somehow everyone knows anyway.
There is a cake, slightly lopsided. There are candles, slightly too many. There is a song, slightly out of tune. {Crew} pretends to be embarrassed and is not embarrassed at all.

episodes.title: The lost sock
text: A single sock has been found in the engine room. Nobody will claim it.

A full investigation takes the whole session. Suspects are interviewed. Alibis are checked. The sock is examined under the microscope. In the end, the case is closed without a culprit, and the sock is given a place of honour on the galley wall.

episodes.title: Letters
text: A mail drone catches up with the ship, three months late, with a small bundle of letters.

Everyone takes theirs to a quiet corner. For a while the ship is very still. Somebody laughs out loud at something. Somebody sniffs. {Crew} reads {crew.their} letter four times and then puts it under {crew.their} pillow.

episodes.title: Bread
text: {Crew} decides to bake bread, properly, from scratch, for the first time.

It takes all session: mixing, kneading, waiting, worrying, waiting more. The whole ship starts to smell like a kitchen on a winter morning. When it comes out of the oven it is dense and slightly burnt and absolutely the best thing anyone has eaten in weeks.

episodes.title: The window seat
text: There is one good window seat on the ship, and today, for once, nobody is in it.
{Crew} takes it with a book and a blanket and a cup of tea, and watches the stars go by, and reads three pages in the whole session, and is completely happy.

episodes.title: Snow in orbit
text: The ship passes through the tail of an icy comet, and for an hour the windows are full of snow: tiny bright flakes of ice drifting past in the dark.
Everybody presses their faces to the glass like children. {Crew} draws a snowflake on the window in the fog of {crew.their} breath.

episodes.title: Mending
text: Everybody brings out the things that need mending: a torn sleeve, a loose button, a jumper with a hole in the elbow. They sit in a circle in the galley and mend together, and talk about nothing, and it takes all session.
Afterwards, everything is a little bit more patched, and everyone is a little bit closer.

episodes.title: Stargazing
text: The ship's lights go off for one hour, on purpose, and everybody lies on the floor of the observation deck in the dark.
There are so many stars it is almost loud. {Crew} points out a constellation {crew.they} {crew:has|have} made up, and explains it in great detail, and by the end everybody can see it.

episodes.title: The plant
text: The little plant on the galley windowsill has flowered. Just one flower, tiny and pale and smelling faintly of somewhere nobody has been.
Nobody remembers who planted it. Everybody takes credit. {Crew} waters it twice that evening, just to be sure.

episodes.title: A quiet day
text: Nothing happens today. The ship hums. The stars go by. Somebody hums along with the ship. Meals are eaten. Books are read. Nobody needs anything.
At the end of it, {Crew} writes one line in the ship's log: "A good day." It is the whole entry.
